steps.title: Lower Austria
steps.body: Grüner grows mainly in Niederösterreich, Lower Austria, along the Danube and to the north. Weinviertel, the largest region, makes peppery, fresh Grüner; it was Austria's first DAC, in 2003. The Wachau, Kremstal and Kamptal make powerful, structured versions on steep terraces. Vienna also grows it.

steps.title: DAC
steps.body: Austria's DAC system, Districtus Austriae Controllatus, ties regions to typical grapes and styles. A Weinviertel DAC is Grüner Veltliner; Kamptal DAC and Kremstal DAC are Grüner or Riesling. Labels can add Reserve for riper, fuller wines. The Wachau uses its own terms: Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd.

steps.prompt: Match each Austrian term to its meaning.
steps.explanation: Austria labels by region and style.

steps.title: Abroad
steps.body: Grüner Veltliner is spreading: Slovakia and Czech Republic grow it, and New Zealand, Australia's Adelaide Hills, the US and England have new plantings. Cool to moderate climates suit it best, keeping its freshness and pepper.

options: A system linking regions to typical grapes and styles
